To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mechanism of interaction of aminooxyl compounds with sheep liver SHMT is similar to that of O-amino D-serine and a minooxyacetic acids, the carboxyl moiety of the inhibitors enhances their rate of interaction with the enzyme, and the identity of the oximes formed from the inhibitors was established.

methoxyamine, like O-amino-D serine and aminoxyacetic acid, is an irreversible inhibitor of sheep liver serin hydroxymethyl transferase (SHMT) by reacting with the pyridoxal phosphate-Schiff base at the active sites.

methoxyamine, the simplest aminooxy inhibitor, interacts with pyridoxalphosphate-Schiff base at the active center of serine hydroxylmethyltransferase and the reaction involves two steps, the first being very fast and the second being a slow unimolecular reaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of action of aminooxygenation and the role of aminooxidation in the metabolism of amino acids.
the mechanism of inhibition of SHMT by aminooxy derivatives of amino acids and the structural requirements for this interaction.
the interactions of aminoxyl and aminooxyl derivatives with the enzyme.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the aminooxy derivatives of alpha-amino acids are competitive inhibitors of sheep liver SHMT and that the carbanion of the aminooxyl group is the species that interacts with the active site of the enzyme.
the aminooxy group of the inhibitors interacts with the pyridoxal phosphate Schiff base of serine hydroxyl-methyltransferase, resulting in the formation of an oxime.
methoxyamine reacts with the enzyme-Schifff base at the active sites of the enzyme to form a Schiff's base intermediate, which is converted to the oxime.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the interaction of aminooxyl compounds with the enzyme proceeds via two steps, one involving the initial formation of a Schiff base and a second involving a rapid conversion of this intermediate to an oxime.
the aminooxy group interacts with the enzyme Schiff base in the first step and the carboxylate group interacts with the pyridoxal phosphate in the second step.

The main takeaway from our work is that
aminooxy derivatives are excellent tools to study enzyme mechanisms.
the mechanism of inhibition by methoxyamine is the same as that of O-amino- D-serine and a similar mechanism can also be expected for hydroxylamine.
methoxyamine is a useful probe for studying the interactions of SHMT with aminooxy inhibitors.
